pages.text: Rows of persimmons hung under the shed eaves behind the house, wrinkled and dry: dried persimmons. Thick snow kept piling up in front of the shed.
"We'll eat these all winter." Grandma held up one finger. "One a day."
Yuki picked one. It was chewy and sweet. "I want just one more."
Yuki picked several at once and wrapped them in their scarf. "Today, I'll pick them all."
Yuki waddled across the snow. The scarf sagged. Momo buried their nose in the snow and sniffed.
Standing before the shed, Yuki opened the scarf. Only two persimmons remained.
Looking back showed only snow. More kept falling, covering every place they had dropped. "Where did they fall?"
Grandma looked at the snow before the shed. "Snow hides everything that falls."
The next day, Yuki picked only one persimmon. The scarf stayed around their neck.
Many persimmons still hung under the shed eaves. Yuki pointed to them one by one and counted.
